objective.text: Invalidate a reset token after a successful password reset.

difficulty.rationale: Trace token lifecycle after the reset callback completes successfully.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

stem: A valid broker reset invokes its callback, the callback stores the new password and returns normally. What happens to that token’s repository record?

options.text: It remains usable until its original expiry regardless of the successful reset.
options.rationale: That ignores the broker’s post-reset token deletion.
options.misconception: That ignores the broker’s post-reset token deletion.

options.text: It is deleted, so a later reset cannot reuse the same token.
options.rationale: The broker deletes the user’s token record after successful callback completion.

options.text: Its lifetime is extended so the user can repeat the same reset if needed.
options.rationale: A successful reset does not renew the token for reuse.
options.misconception: A successful reset does not renew the token for reuse.

options.text: Its plaintext value is copied into the user’s remember_token field automatically.
options.rationale: Reset-token cleanup and remember-token handling are different concerns; this is not the broker’s automatic action.
options.misconception: Reset-token cleanup and remember-token handling are different concerns; this is not the broker’s automatic action.
